meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'очный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('juicy; succulent').

examples.text: Мясо должно стать мягким и сочным.
examples.trans: The meat must become tender and juicy.

examples.text: Но сочные мясные котлеты такие вкусные!
examples.trans: But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!

examples.text: Мясо получилось очень нежным и сочным.
examples.trans: The meat turned out very tender and juicy.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('marbled (beef), marble').

examples.trans: Of juicy marbled beef.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень мраморный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very marbled day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Beef, liver.

examples.text: И ещё был торт из говядины!
examples.trans: And there was also a cake made of beef!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in front of, before', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'punishment, retribution' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Перед карой молодого ягненка не устоит никто.
examples.trans: Nobody can resist a rack of young lamb.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая кара.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new punishment.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('young').

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?
They have a young family.

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'lamb' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a young and tasty lamb.

examples.text: Зачем обижаешь? Это молодой и вкусный ягнёнок!
examples.trans: Why insult me? This is a young and tasty lamb!
Yes, this lamb is really good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'стоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to resist, hold one's ground'.

examples.text: Перед карой молодого ягненка не устоит никто.
examples.trans: Nobody can resist a rack of young lamb.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет устоять без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to resist without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody will come in.
I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer, to suggest', paired with 'предлагать'.

examples.trans: But you were offered a job.
He offered coffee.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: But you were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
Good! Everything's fine over there.
All right, I'll be there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'жаренный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('well-done, roasted through').

examples.text: Вам не предложат хорошо прожаренный стейк.
examples.trans: They will not offer you a well-done steak.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень прожаренный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very well-done day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тейк'). Common masculine noun meaning 'steak' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть немного подождут свои горячие стейки.
examples.trans: Let them wait a bit for their hot steaks.

examples.text: Вот вкусный французский стейк и горячая рыба.
examples.trans: Here is a delicious French steak and hot fish.
Just like your steak from yesterday!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ужели').

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?
Do you really not care at all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone, somebody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'казаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to refuse, decline, renounce', paired with 'отказываться'.

examples.trans: He refused to sign the report.
She declined the offered money.
Really? Did he refuse to sign it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from; of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A letter from Mum.
I'm tired of work.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'miracle, wonder' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a culinary miracle!

examples.text: Потому что это настоящее кулинарное чудо!
examples.trans: Because it is a real culinary miracle!
Just wait for a miracle.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did you forget, or what?
I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Say something.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.
Are you doing anything about it?

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('vegetarian').

examples.text: Скажите, а нет ли у вас чего-нибудь вегетарианского?
examples.trans: Tell me, do you have anything vegetarian?
Agreed, vegetarians are total idiots too.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vegetarian' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a strict vegetarian.

examples.text: Вегетарианцы — это люди, которые не едят мясо.
examples.trans: Vegetarians are people who do not eat meat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'meat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?
Very tasty meat!

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'grandmother; old woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: My grandmother lives in the village.
That's better than the old lady.
Yes, but better than the old lady.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'house; building; home' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There's a new building on Simashko Street.
This is my home.

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лезный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('useful, helpful').

examples.trans: Useful advice.
Give me some useful advice.
Very useful plans.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.
What delicious tea!

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втрак'). Common masculine noun meaning 'breakfast' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are having a romantic breakfast here.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на завтрак?
examples.trans: What do we have for breakfast today?

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.trans: This is the best day!
You're my best friend.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'paris' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We recently returned from Paris.
I still work as a cook.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant, nice').

examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!
He's a very nice person.
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'appetite' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!
He has a good appetite.
Your porridge. Enjoy your meal.
